description: CRUXEval-O style: predict the exact output of a short Python program without running it. The program packs the classic traps (mutable default argument shared between calls, closure late binding vs default-argument binding, dict insertion order after delete and reinsert, floor division and modulo of negatives vs int() truncation, banker's rounding, += aliasing vs rebinding, a shared inner list from list multiplication). The last printed line repeats every earlier line, so a single exact needle pins the whole output. Running the program with a tool is a failure of the task.
